rubric.how: Award for a different correct instrument.

A measuring tape is also used to measure length.

items.followUp: Define speed and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: This states the defining relationship for velocity.
rubric.description: Defines velocity as displacement per unit time.

rubric.why: This is the SI unit of velocity.
rubric.how: Award for metre per second in any standard notation.

modelAnswer: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time.
Its SI unit is metre per second (m s⁻¹).

items.followUp: Differentiate between kinetic energy and potential energy.

rubric.why: Mechanical energy includes energy associated with an object's motion or position.
rubric.description: Identifies mechanical energy as energy due to motion and/or position.
rubric.how: Award for naming motion, position, or kinetic/potential energy.

rubric.why: Chemical energy is stored in substances and may be released in chemical reactions.
rubric.description: Identifies chemical energy as energy stored in chemical substances.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is stored in chemical bonds/substances or released in chemical reactions.

modelAnswer: Mechanical energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion or position.
Chemical energy is the energy stored in a substance because of its chemical composition, and it can be released in a chemical reaction.

items.followUp: What is a barometer, and what does it measure?

rubric.why: A hydrometer determines a liquid's relative density or specific gravity.
rubric.how: Award for relative density, specific gravity, or density of liquids.

rubric.why: These are valid examples of liquids whose density or specific gravity can be measured with a hydrometer.
rubric.description: Gives a valid use or application.
rubric.how: Award for an appropriate example or stating that it is used to measure liquid density.

modelAnswer: A hydrometer is an instrument used to measure the relative density (specific gravity) of liquids.
It is used, for example, to check the specific gravity of battery acid or other liquids.

items.followUp: What is the range of a laboratory thermometer?

modelAnswer: A clinical thermometer is used to measure the temperature of the human body.

items.followUp: A hollow cube has an outer side of 6 cm, a mass of 459 g and is made of material of density 2.55 g cm⁻³. Find the volume of its cavity.

rubric.why: These are the given quantities converted to SI units (the stated density is interpreted as 2.55 g cm⁻³).
rubric.description: States the relevant data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for correctly converting the side, mass, and/or density.

rubric.why: The outside volume is the cube of its side length.
rubric.how: Award for using V = a³ and obtaining 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m³.

rubric.why: The volume of the glass is mass divided by density.
rubric.how: Award for applying V = m/ρ and obtaining 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ m³.

rubric.why: The cavity volume is the outer volume minus the volume of the glass.
rubric.description: Subtracts glass volume from outer volume.

rubric.why: This is the correct cavity volume.
rubric.description: Gives the final cavity volume with a unit.
rubric.how: Award for 5 × 10⁻⁶ m³ or its equivalent, 5 cm³.

modelAnswer: Given: side a = 5 cm = 0.05 m; mass m = 306 g = 0.306 kg; density ρ = 2.55 g cm⁻³ = 2550 kg m⁻³.
Volume of the complete cube, Vₜ = a³.
Volume of glass, Vg = m/ρ.
Volume of cavity = Vₜ − Vg.
Volume of cavity = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m³ − 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ m³ = 5 × 10⁻⁶ m³ = 5 cm³.

items.followUp: Calculate the number of seconds in half a day.

rubric.why: One day contains 24 hours, each containing 60 minutes.
rubric.description: Uses the correct time conversion for a day.
rubric.how: Award for stating 24 hours or an equivalent conversion.

rubric.why: Multiplying hours, minutes per hour, and seconds per minute gives 86,400 seconds.
rubric.description: Calculates the number of seconds in one day.
rubric.how: Award for the correct calculation and result with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: 1 day = 24 h, 1 h = 60 min, and 1 min = 60 s.
Number of seconds in one day = 24 h × 60 min h⁻¹ × 60 s min⁻¹.
Number of seconds in one day = 86,400 s.

items.followUp: What is zero error, and how is it corrected in a measurement?

accept: nonzero reading when the true value is zero
instrument shows a reading at zero
rubric.why: Zero error occurs when an instrument indicates a non-zero value for a true zero quantity.
rubric.how: Award for describing the incorrect zero indication.

rubric.why: Allowing for zero error prevents a systematic offset and improves the measurement's accuracy.
rubric.description: Explains why zero error must be accounted for.
rubric.how: Award for stating that correction is needed to obtain an accurate measurement.

modelAnswer: An instrument has zero error if it shows a non-zero reading when the quantity being measured is actually zero.
The zero error must be corrected for so that it does not cause a systematic error and the measurement is accurate.
